response.reason: This lens compares the exact author-source-derived NL contracts against the closed FCSTM transition/state inventory for endpoint identity, initial-entry ownership, and guard-disjointness structure, focusing on wrong/missing targets and unauthorized/collapsed edges. The FCSTM root uses a routed macro pattern (R45RouteToken) instead of literal named-target edges, so many DoorOpenWithItem-scoped transitions (NL4-NL8) are exit-to-[*] edges guarded by route tokens rather than direct named-target edges; the macro/source_trace mapping ties each such exit back to one source transition, so per working-contract macro-join discipline these are treated as satisfied through the traced macro rather than flagged as wrong-target, except where the closed model's actual resolved target diverges from the NL target even after macro resolution. After checking each endpoint: NL1-INITENTRY-1 root->DoorShut initial edge is present and reachable (transition:line:56/tr_0001), satisfied, omitted. NL1-ENDPOINT-1 and NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (duplicate DoorShut->DoorOpen on door opened) are satisfied by transition:line:57. NL2-ENDPOINT-2 DoorOpen->DoorShut on door closed: satisfied by transition:line:58. NL3 endpoints satisfied via macro DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem/DoorIdleWithItem. NL4-NL8 endpoints resolve correctly through the route-token macro chain per source_trace joins. Guard-disjointness contracts (NL4-DISJOINT-1, NL1-DERIVED, NL8-DERIVED) remain predicate-null W1 candidates in general, but structurally the DoorShut group's disjointness contract depends on a genuine missing alternative: the complete transition inventory for DoorShut has only one outgoing edge (Door_Opened->DoorOpen); no Cancel-triggered self-loop edge exists anywhere in exact_source_inventory.transitions or inspection_equivalent_facts for source=DoorShut, and the PlantUML/FCSTM text 'DoorShut : Cancel' / 'DoorShut\\n[PlantUML body] Cancel' is only a state body annotation, not an edge. This is a complete-inventory absence, so I emit an S2 missing-edge candidate for NL1-SELFLOOP-1 bound to the existing DoorShut state ref on both sides (no self-loop edge exists to supply its own ref). All other endpoint contracts (NL2 through NL8) are satisfied through the traced macro/token structure and are omitted from candidates, as is NL1-INITENTRY-1 (satisfied root->DoorShut initial edge) and NL1-DERIVED guard-disjointness contract for DoorShut (since the two 'alternatives' NL describes are the self-loop, which does not structurally exist as a distinguishable transition, but this deeper issue is fully captured by the missing-edge candidate on NL1-SELFLOOP-1 itself; emitting a second disjointness candidate for the same root defect would duplicate the same locus/property gap, so it is omitted here for this lens and left to the effect/behavior lens if independently warranted).

All 11 states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts.metrics, so no root-reachability defect exists. All declared events have a reachable consumer per event_consumers list, so no consumer-coverage gap exists. I omit all satisfied endpoint/effect/entry contracts from candidates and unresolved per sparse-response discipline.

branches.reason: This lens compares the exact author-source-derived NL contracts against the closed FCSTM transition/state inventory for endpoint identity, initial-entry ownership, and guard-disjointness structure, focusing on wrong/missing targets and unauthorized/collapsed edges. The FCSTM root uses a routed macro pattern (R45RouteToken) instead of literal named-target edges, so many DoorOpenWithItem-scoped transitions (NL4-NL8) are exit-to-[*] edges guarded by route tokens rather than direct named-target edges; the macro/source_trace mapping ties each such exit back to one source transition, so per working-contract macro-join discipline these are treated as satisfied through the traced macro rather than flagged as wrong-target, except where the closed model's actual resolved target diverges from the NL target even after macro resolution. After checking each endpoint: NL1-INITENTRY-1 root->DoorShut initial edge is present and reachable (transition:line:56/tr_0001), satisfied, omitted. NL1-ENDPOINT-1 and NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (duplicate DoorShut->DoorOpen on door opened) are satisfied by transition:line:57. NL2-ENDPOINT-2 DoorOpen->DoorShut on door closed: satisfied by transition:line:58. NL3 endpoints satisfied via macro DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem/DoorIdleWithItem. NL4-NL8 endpoints resolve correctly through the route-token macro chain per source_trace joins. Guard-disjointness contracts (NL4-DISJOINT-1, NL1-DERIVED, NL8-DERIVED) remain predicate-null W1 candidates in general, but structurally the DoorShut group's disjointness contract depends on a genuine missing alternative: the complete transition inventory for DoorShut has only one outgoing edge (Door_Opened->DoorOpen); no Cancel-triggered self-loop edge exists anywhere in exact_source_inventory.transitions or inspection_equivalent_facts for source=DoorShut, and the PlantUML/FCSTM text 'DoorShut : Cancel' / 'DoorShut\\n[PlantUML body] Cancel' is only a state body annotation, not an edge. This is a complete-inventory absence, so I emit an S2 missing-edge candidate for NL1-SELFLOOP-1 bound to the existing DoorShut state ref on both sides (no self-loop edge exists to supply its own ref). All other endpoint contracts (NL2 through NL8) are satisfied through the traced macro/token structure and are omitted from candidates, as is NL1-INITENTRY-1 (satisfied root->DoorShut initial edge) and NL1-DERIVED guard-disjointness contract for DoorShut (since the two 'alternatives' NL describes are the self-loop, which does not structurally exist as a distinguishable transition, but this deeper issue is fully captured by the missing-edge candidate on NL1-SELFLOOP-1 itself; emitting a second disjointness candidate for the same root defect would duplicate the same locus/property gap, so it is omitted here for this lens and left to the effect/behavior lens if independently warranted).
